title: Recover and watch the deficit

predict.q: The economy has a **negative output gap of 4%**. The deficit is **4% of GDP**. The economy recovers to its potential output. Tax rates and spending plans do not change. What happens to the deficit?

options.s: It disappears completely, because recovery fixes the public finances.
options.fb: Recovery removes only the cyclical part; the structural deficit comes from tax and spending choices.

options.s: It stays at 4%, because the government made no new decision.
options.fb: No decision is needed for the cyclical part: tax revenue rises and benefit spending falls on their own.

options.s: It falls, but part of it remains.
options.fb: The cyclical part (2%) goes as the gap closes; the 2% structural deficit remains.

options.s: It rises, because a growing economy needs more public spending.
options.fb: In a recovery fewer people claim benefits and tax revenue rises, so the deficit falls.

task: Move the **output gap** slider to 0, then to +2%, and watch the cyclical and structural parts of the deficit bar.

target.do: Move the output gap slider to 0, then press Check.

takeaway: Recovery removes the **cyclical** deficit; the **structural** deficit needs a policy decision.
